newsitem.title: USA: Music industry to hold Latin trade fair in Miami.
newsitem.headline: Music industry to hold Latin trade fair in Miami.

text.p: The music industry organization MIDEM has launched a new Latin American and Caribbean division to promote the music that "makes the world dance" and will stage a big trade fair and festival in Miami next year.

"With its extraordinary wonderful and bicultural atmosphere, Miami has become the very heart of the Latin entertainment industry," MIDEM chief executive Xavier Roy told a news conference on Monday night.
"This is why we are proud to launch here the very first MIDEM Latin American and Caribbean Music Market."

MIDEM's annual event in Cannes, France, draws thousands of music industry agents, publishers, musicians and executives looking to sign deals and negotiate rights worth millions of dollars. Two years ago it opened MIDEM Asia, based in Hong Kong, to promote the Asian music business.
In Latin America and the Caribbean, "music is more than a cultural phenomenon, it's a way of life," Roy said.

"This way of life is reflected by a multitude of musical styles -- salsa, samba, socca, merengue, tejano, bailantes, Rock en Espanol and reggae to mention just a few," he said. "All of these styles make the whole world dance."
The Latin American market has been fragmented and locally orientated, he said. MIDEM intended to help artists gain more international attention and businessmen market the product more widely.
An economic boom and ever younger population in Latin America had created a huge demand for music, he said.
The MIDEM Latin American and Caribbean Music Market will be held next Sept. 8-11. About 2,500 people are expected to attend, and more than 40 acts are scheduled to perform.
MIDEM stands for the International Record, Music Publishing and Video Music Market.
